object_description: rectangular block with a horizontally bisected volume over a solid gymnasium base
geometry_property: solid base with lightweight upper floors
design_condition: the block replaces the old gymnasiums with its narrow side towards the schoolyard and its long side defining the street space, set respectfully into the wooded slope and surrounded by green embankments

positive: The narrow side borders the schoolyard while the long side defines the street space, keeping distance from the existing wing
The schoolyard can be overlooked across the site, creating a spatial continuum extending to the sports fields
The striking slope edge is dealt with in an interesting way and could be developed further along the street
Landscaping and tree planting create a strong interlocking of settlement and landscape space
The wide staircase connecting the levels is clearly part of the landscape, so one crosses the semi-shaded slope edge
Green embankments conceal the equipment rooms and set the building respectfully into the wooded slope
Relocating the parking better embeds the existing wing in the quarter
The horizontal bisection clearly defines the two main uses from outside
The concrete lower half is skilfully attached to the neighbouring building while the upper half appears open and light
With three storeys reaching only to the eaves of the historic wing, that building retains its main role
The area behind the historic wing is designed as playground and outdoor classroom, a landscaped counterpoint to the austere architecture
The entrance leads into a large, clearly structured foyer lit by a skylight
Library and games room have external doors for use outside school hours
The studio zones are supplied with daylight via the central atrium, which makes them very usable
The triple gymnasium is well lit and well organised
Interventions in the existing buildings are proportionate and create new qualities
The timber-concrete composite construction and central atrium reduce the loads on the gym ceiling girders
Heterogeneous subsoil and groundwater are addressed with plausible concepts
A site-specific solution of great spatial quality, with a very carefully elaborated open space concept
The clear structural concept, spacious hall, atrium and material choice give user-friendly interiors with architectural quality
negative: The foyer appearance does not suggest a primary school building
The dining rooms are constricted by the adjoining room layer and are only just sufficiently accessible
The lift is too far from the delivery area and the kitchen, and storage space is lacking
An undesirable mix of school, childcare and auditorium operations occurs on the access floor
The attractiveness of the ground floor disappears when the folding walls are closed, turning it labyrinthine and dark
The choice of a block with an inner courtyard is hardly understandable on the outskirts of the town
The conflict between outside access and the clean corridor is unresolved and the checkrooms are too small
The size of the classrooms and the layout of the group rooms in the existing wing do not meet operational requirements
The workroom and multi-purpose room by the kindergarten are not yet operationally resolved
The settlement of the volume requires considerable excavation and excavation pit support
The kitchen and childcare area on the ground floor is constricted by the structure
The solution can be perceived as not being site-specific enough
